solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Crazy American on The Strand in an open car

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece set on another follows it, so the crazy word comes after the shore word

parts.note: a strand is a shore, so the strand here is a beach
buggy is American slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A mad American is driving a convertible along London's famous Strand.
explanation.walkthrough: The Strand looks like the London street, but a strand is simply a shore.
explanation.definitionFit: A beach buggy is a light, roofless vehicle built for driving over sand.

clue.text: Eastern nation worried public schoolboy

indicators.note: worried suggests something agitated and turned over, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A nation in the east is troubled by a boy from an elite school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eastern' and 'nation' look like one phrase, but Eastern supplies only its initial letter; 'worried' scrambles the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An Etonian is a pupil of Eton College, the most famous English public (fee-paying) school.

clue.text: Examine a pattern of squares

definitions.meaning: to look over or inspect something
a chequered design, as on a tartan or gingham

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to inspect and a design of alternating coloured squares.

clue.text: French port wine

definitions.meaning: a city and harbour on the Garonne in south-west France
the red or white wine from that region, claret among them

explanation.definitionFit: Bordeaux is a major port city in France and also the name of the wine made around it.

clue.text: Let the cat out of the bag, so resign?

definitions.text: Let the cat out of the bag
definitions.meaning: to reveal a secret by accident
a player who resigns concedes the match, handing over the contest

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means betraying a secret, and read literally it describes conceding a contest.

clue.text: Cowardly one may if struck

definitions.meaning: someone hit might shout out a cry of pain, read as two words, a shout and an ouch

explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for cowardly, and split in two it is what a person struck might do: cry out in pain.

clue.text: Hence appearing in Mother Goose

indicators.note: appearing in says the letters show up inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Therefore it turns up in a nursery rhyme book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing in' points to the letters spanning motHER GOose.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for therefore, a formal synonym of hence.

clue.text: Found stable groomed one's horses only initially

indicators.note: grooming tidies and rearranges, so the letters of stable are reordered

parts.note: one is I, and one's is I plus the S of is

indicators.note: only initially means just the first letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A stable has been tidied and its horses groomed, at least at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groomed' rearranges STABLE into ESTABL; 'only initially' takes H from horses.
explanation.definitionFit: To found an institution is to establish it, set it up for the first time.

clue.text: Adult class includes heartless woman

indicators.note: includes means the class word holds the next piece within it

parts.note: a class is a group of people sharing something

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle, leaving only the outside letters of woman

explanation.surface: A class of grown-ups contains a woman with no heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the whole middle of woman, not just one letter, keeping only its first and last.
explanation.definitionFit: A grown-up is an adult, someone fully mature.

clue.text: Accomplished English poet, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: John Donne, the 17th-century metaphysical poet

explanation.surface: An accomplished English poet, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done has been completed or accomplished.

clue.text: NT book, English version, acquired by member of the family

indicators.note: acquired by means the first pieces are taken inside the family word

parts.note: a relation is a family member
V is the abbreviation for version, as in Bible editions

explanation.surface: A relative obtains an English translation of a New Testament book.
explanation.walkthrough: EV goes after the R of RELATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Revelation is the final book of the New Testament.

clue.text: Relish best left close to plate

parts.note: the pick of something is the best of it

indicators.note: close to means the last letter, the end, of plate

explanation.surface: The best relish is left near the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' looks like nearby but takes the E ending plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickle is a preserved condiment, a kind of relish.

clue.text: Robot men reassembled with brass instrument

indicators.note: something reassembled is put back together in a new form, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Robot men have been rebuilt carrying a brass instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The trombone is a brass instrument with a sliding tube.

clue.text: Vulnerable at home? Then see about vicious dog

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: about means the word see goes round the dog

parts.note: taken as written
a cur is a nasty, snappish dog

explanation.surface: Feeling exposed at home? Then watch out for the savage dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark splits the clue in two; 'Then' is just a link joining the home piece to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To be insecure is to be unprotected and open to harm, vulnerable.

clue.text: Sequacious aide yells out

indicators.note: out means the letters are out of their order, to be reordered

explanation.surface: A deputy bellows out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges AIDEYELLS. Sequacious is a rare word meaning inclined to follow others.
explanation.definitionFit: Sequacious describes one who follows unthinkingly, someone readily swayed.

clue.text: I spot game

definitions.meaning: I see something, said in the first person
a children's guessing game played on journeys

explanation.definitionFit: I spy means I see, and is also a guessing game played by children.

clue.text: Vigorous daily sex may result in a form of blindness

indicators.note: vigorous suggests energetic tossing about, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: An old wives' tale warns that energetic daily sex could make you go blind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vigorous' rearranges DAILYSEX. Dyslexia was once called word blindness.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyslexia was formerly called word blindness, a difficulty reading written text.

clue.text: See 19
Exaggerate to excess about, for example, onset of gout

parts.note: over means about, as in arguing over something

indicators.note: onset of means the very first letter of gout

explanation.surface: Overdoing it, regarding rich food for instance, may start the gout.
explanation.definitionFit: To overegg the pudding is to overdo or embellish something too much.

clue.text: Song in the gay jazzy musical

indicators.note: jazzy suggests lively improvisation, so the letters are jazzed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A number from a flamboyant jazz show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jazzy' rearranges SONGINTHEGAY; the answer runs from 19 to 17 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything Goes is Cole Porter's 1934 musical comedy, also the title of its song.

clue.text: Coin is a counterfeit from a Mediterranean city

indicators.note: counterfeit means forged, so the letters are recast in a new order

explanation.surface: A forged coin is from a Mediterranean city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital of Cyprus, an island in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Carried round Pacific island

parts.note: borne is the past participle of bear, to carry
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Carried around a Pacific island.
explanation.definitionFit: Borneo is a large island in the western Pacific region, in the Malay Archipelago.

clue.text: Words of praise for how a steak may have been cooked

definitions.text: how a steak may have been cooked
definitions.meaning: cooked right through, with no pink inside

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a congratulation and also describes meat cooked thoroughly.

clue.text: Son to ring back about current trees

indicators.note: to means the son letter is added to the end of the rest
about means the reversed word goes around the next piece
back means the word call is read backwards

parts.note: to ring is to call on the phone
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A son phones back about the flow of trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses CALL to LLAC, which goes round I, then S follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilacs are flowering shrubs or small trees of the olive family.

clue.text: One's landed in Scotland

parts.note: read as someone who has arrived by air, but landed means owning land: a Scottish property owner

explanation.definitionFit: A laird is a Scottish landowner, a member of the landed gentry.

clue.text: Sounds like maximum increase in production of a resinous substance

indicators.note: sounds like means the words are as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: a ceiling is a maximum, and to wax is to increase

explanation.surface: The highest growth in output of a resin.
explanation.walkthrough: CEILING (maximum) and WAX (increase, as the moon waxes) are said together.
explanation.definitionFit: Sealing wax is a resin-based compound once melted to seal letters.

clue.text: Casablanca's Ms Lund, some devil's advocate

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Ingrid Bergman's character in the film plays devil's advocate.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilsa Lund is the heroine played by Ingrid Bergman in the film Casablanca.

clue.text: Elderly French artist almost returned

indicators.note: returned means the shortened name is read backwards
almost means the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Edgar Degas, the French Impressionist painter

explanation.surface: An elderly French painter has nearly come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims DEGAS to DEGA; 'returned' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged means old, of advanced years.

clue.text: Egyptian king, stupid losing head, vassal reported back

indicators.note: losing head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: dozy means slow-witted or stupid
a man was a feudal vassal, a liegeman

indicators.note: back means the word said is read backwards

parts.note: said means reported

explanation.surface: A dim pharaoh is beheaded while a subject reports back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' cuts DOZY to OZY; 'back' reverses SAID to DIAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozymandias is the Greek name for Ramesses II, the subject of Shelley's sonnet.
